thought_title: The Voice from Heaven and Polycarp's First Confession
orientation: Polycarp has just been led into the stadium amid a great uproar, and now as he enters, a voice from heaven speaks to him, after which the proconsul begins his interrogation.
pass_a_gloss: And to Polycarp entering into the stadium a voice from heaven came: Be strong, Polycarp, and act like a man. And the one who spoke no one saw, but the voice those of our people who were present heard. And then, when he was brought forward, there was a great uproar of those who heard that Polycarp had been arrested. So when he was brought forward, the proconsul asked him whether he himself was Polycarp. And when he confessed, he tried to persuade [him] to deny, saying: Have respect for your age, and other things following these, as it is their custom to say: Swear by Caesar's fortune, repent, say: Away with the atheists. But Polycarp, with a stern face looking at the whole crowd of lawless nations in the stadium and shaking his hand at them, and groaning and looking up to heaven, said: Away with the atheists. And when the proconsul pressed and said: Swear, and I release you, revile Christ, Polycarp said: Eighty-six years I have served him, and he has wronged me in nothing: and how can I blaspheme my king who saved me?

choices.why: The imperative carries the sense of courage and manly resolve; 'act like a man' preserves the gendered force of the Greek verb without modernizing it away.
The genitive plural of the possessive adjective refers to fellow Christians; 'our people' keeps the insider perspective of the Smyrnaean church.
The phrase is a fixed polemical expression for pagans; 'lawless nations' preserves the biblical resonance of the Greek.
The dative of manner describes Polycarp's grave, weighty expression; 'stern face' captures the seriousness without over-dramatizing.
The present tense in Greek expresses an action continuing from the past into the present; the English perfect 'have served' conveys this duration.

choices.term: τὸν βασιλέα μου τὸν σώσαντά με
choices.why: The articular participle with the aorist points to a completed act of salvation; 'who saved me' keeps the aorist force.

pass_b_english: As Polycarp entered the stadium, a voice came from heaven: "Be strong, Polycarp, and act like a man." No one saw who spoke, but those of our people who were present heard the voice. Then, when he was brought forward, there was a great uproar from those who heard that Polycarp had been arrested.

When he was brought before him, the proconsul asked whether he was Polycarp. When he admitted it, the proconsul tried to persuade him to deny it, saying, "Have respect for your age," and other things that follow from this, as they customarily say: "Swear by Caesar's fortune, repent, say, 'Away with the atheists.'" But Polycarp looked with a stern face at the whole crowd of lawless nations in the stadium, shook his hand at them, groaned, looked up to heaven, and said, "Away with the atheists."

The proconsul pressed him and said, "Swear, and I release you; revile Christ." Polycarp replied, "For eighty-six years I have served him, and he has done me no wrong. How can I blaspheme my king who saved me?"

problems.quote: When he was brought before him, the proconsul asked whether he was Polycarp.
problems.why: Two 'he/him' pronouns in one clause; referents are unclear.
problems.fix: Specify: 'When Polycarp was brought before the proconsul.'

edits.old: When he was brought before him, the proconsul asked whether he was Polycarp.
edits.new: When Polycarp was brought before the proconsul, the proconsul asked whether he was Polycarp.

problems.why: Polycarp speaks this, but crowd also shouts similar; reader may miss he turns their cry back on them.
problems.fix: Clarify attribution: 'Polycarp said to the crowd...'

problems.quote: Be strong, Polycarp, and act like a man
problems.why: Echoes Joshua 1:6-7, 9 or 1 Corinthians 16:13, but not exact quotation; presented as heavenly voice.
problems.fix: Note: allusion to biblical language, not direct citation.

edits.old: But Polycarp looked with a stern face at the whole crowd of lawless nations in the stadium, shook his hand at them, groaned, looked up to heaven, and said, "Away with the atheists."
edits.new: But Polycarp looked with a stern face at the whole crowd of lawless nations in the stadium, shook his hand at them, groaned, looked up to heaven, and said to the crowd, "Away with the atheists."

fixed: The 'Be strong, Polycarp, and act like a man' problem is not a translation error; the English already renders the source accurately as a heavenly voice, and the source itself is an allusion rather than a direct citation, so no change is needed.

problems.why: Same Roman authority is called both “proconsul” and “police captain”.
Unclear whether Polycarp or the crowd utters this phrase.
problems.fix: Attribute the utterance explicitly (e.g., “Polycarp shouted…” or “the crowd shouted…”).

problems.why: Likely a mistranslation; the original martyrdom text says “Away with the Jews!” or a similar phrase.
problems.fix: Replace with the historically accurate wording.

edits.old: When Polycarp was brought before the proconsul, the proconsul asked whether he was Polycarp.
edits.new: When Polycarp was brought before him, the proconsul asked whether he was Polycarp.

edits.old: But Polycarp looked with a stern face at the whole crowd of lawless nations in the stadium, shook his hand at them, groaned, looked up to heaven, and said to the crowd, "Away with the atheists."
edits.new: But Polycarp looked with a stern face at the whole crowd of lawless nations in the stadium, shook his hand at them, groaned, looked up to heaven, and said, "Away with the atheists."

fixed: The glossary issue about 'police captain' does not appear in the provided English text; the English consistently uses 'proconsul'.
The speaker attribution is already explicit in the English: Polycarp says 'Away with the atheists.'
The source text reads 'Αἶρε τοὺς ἀθέους' ('Away with the atheists'), so the English is not a mistranslation.

problems.why: The proconsul is named only in section 21; reader may not connect him to 'the proconsul' throughout.
problems.fix: Name him earlier or note the identification.

edits.old: When Polycarp was brought before him, the proconsul asked whether he was Polycarp.
edits.new: When Polycarp was brought before him, Statius Quadratus the proconsul asked whether he was Polycarp.

fixed: The proconsul is now identified as Statius Quadratus at his first appearance in the narrative, connecting him to the named proconsul in section 21.
